title: Building serverless-first developer experiences at scale
abstract: A deep dive into how developer experience principles apply to serverless architecture — from API design to observability. This talk covers the patterns New Relic uses internally and what AWS Heroes are seeing in production across hundreds of teams.

title: Observability on Serverless — doing more with less noise
abstract: Serverless observability is hard. You can't just SSH into a Lambda. This talk walks through practical patterns for distributed tracing, structured logging, and anomaly detection using New Relic — without drowning in CloudWatch noise.

title: Serverless-first developer experience at scale
abstract: What does it mean to design for developers first? This session explores the intersection of serverless architecture and developer experience — covering IaC patterns, local development workflows, and the feedback loop optimisations that actually move teams faster.

title: Event-driven patterns you might be missing
abstract: EventBridge, SNS, SQS — most teams pick one and stop. This talk covers the composition patterns that unlock real async resilience: saga orchestration, outbox pattern, and event sourcing with DynamoDB Streams. With live code demos.

title: From code to community: the DevRel playbook
abstract: Developer Relations is often misunderstood as marketing with a GitHub account. This talk is a practical playbook for engineers moving into DevRel — how to measure impact, build trust with developer communities, and create content that actually helps.

title: New Relic observability for event-driven serverless systems
abstract: Event-driven systems are notoriously hard to trace. When a Lambda fails three hops from the trigger, how do you find it fast? This talk demonstrates end-to-end distributed tracing for EventBridge + Lambda + DynamoDB using New Relic's APM, with patterns applicable to any observability platform.
